posts.text: If your wallet is small and it’s still not growing, read this. You don’t need bigger trades. You need better risk management. Let’s say you have a $200 wallet. Before entering any trade, decide one thing first: “How much am I okay losing if this trade is wrong?” For example, fix your maximum risk at $5 per trade. Now don’t randomly put $5 as margin and choose 20x leverage. That’s not how it works. First find your entry, then find the technical stop-loss the level where your trade idea becomes invalid. Suppose your SL is 5% away. Maximum risk = $5 SL distance = 5% Position size = $5 ÷ 5% = $100 Only after this calculate the leverage according to the margin you want to use. If you use $10 margin: $100 ÷ $10 = 10x leverage So if the 5% SL gets hit, your planned loss is around $5, not your whole account. On the surface, these two markets look completely unrelated. But underneath, they can react to the same macro pressure. A stronger USD, rising US yields, and Brent pushing above $100 all mean tighter financial conditions and less risk appetite. Gold gets pressured because it doesn’t generate yield. Bitcoin gets pressured because it’s still trading more like a risk asset, with leverage making the move even sharper. Bottom line: when yields and the USD rise together, the market is repricing the real cost of capital and the possibility that the Fed stays restrictive for longer.

posts.text: Anthropic has released FlashProve, an open-source AI inference verification system based on zkSNARKs. According to Odaily, StarkWare co-founder Alessandro Chiesa participated in the research, and the system uses cryptographic methods related to blockchain zero-knowledge technology to let users verify that an AI output came from a specified model without accessing its weights or rerunning it. Anthropic said Claude contributed to optimizing FlashProve and that the code and Lean formal proofs are open source. The system remains a research prototype, with proof generation requiring about 70 to 95 times the GPU compute time of ordinary inference. Tests showed that FlashProve generated proofs for Meta’s 400-billion-parameter Llama 4 Maverick at about 110 tokens per second on a single H100 GPU. Each proof was about 19 MB.

posts.text: BNB Chain has included BEP-706 in its Jenner hard fork, adding a precompiled contract at address 0x70 that lets smart contracts read current block timestamps in milliseconds. According to Odaily, the proposal lets developers retrieve elapsed milliseconds since the Unix epoch; previously, contracts could access only second-level timestamps through block.timestamp, making it impossible to distinguish blocks produced within the same second. The feature can improve precision for time-limited signature quotes, auction deadlines, and checks on price-oracle update timeliness. It is an incremental upgrade and does not change the existing second-level return behavior of block.timestamp.

posts.text: SlowMist Chief Information Security Officer 23pds said claims that CVE-2026-98432 allows zero-click remote root access on all Ubuntu systems are inaccurate. According to Foresight News, the Linux kernel flaw is a use-after-free race in the IPv4 TCP handshake that affects the underlying network protocol stack, not a specific application, and exploitation requires the target server to have an MPTCP listener enabled. Linux does not enable MPTCP by default, so only servers with special configurations are affected. As of October 30, Debian 12 and 13 had released fixes; Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04 and 26.04 were still being patched, while fixes for RHEL 8, 9 and 10 had been postponed. No officially confirmed cases of widespread exploitation in the wild had been reported.

Suleyman said he would call for AI development to pause if consciousness emerged during training, until the trait could be removed. He advocated designing AI without consciousness or intrinsic motives, with the goal of advancing human welfare, and warned that conscious AI could put its own needs first and compete with people for resources.
